title: Swedish Hometown To Honor Rosenqvist With Public Celebration
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
2026 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Felix Rosenqvist will be honored Saturday, Dec. 5 by his hometown, Värnamo, during a public celebration in the Swedish city.

Local residents, motorsports fans and visitors from near and far are invited to join the city in celebrating his historic victory May 24 in the Indianapolis 500. The free, family-friendly event will take place in central Värnamo with Rosenqvist as the guest of honor.

“Celebrating an Indy 500 victory in my hometown will be an unforgettable way to conclude the best year of my life,” Rosenqvist said. “Sharing an occasion like this with everyone in Värnamo, where the dream began, will feel completely surreal. It will truly be one of those pinch-me moments.

“It is truly amazing to think that we will all be able to experience and share this together. I am really looking forward to seeing friends, family and everyone else in Värnamo in December.”

The program will include tributes from the stage, interviews, live music and motorsports-themed activities. Representatives from INDYCAR will take part in the celebration. Additional news and highlights will be announced closer to the event.

Rosenqvist earned his first victory in ”The Greatest Spectacle in Racing” in the No. 60 Honda for Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian. He beat David Malukas of Team Penske by .0233 of a second in the closest finish in the century-plus history of the race.

“Felix Rosenqvist’s success is an outstanding achievement that has inspired tremendous pride and joy throughout Värnamo,” said Staffan Svensson, project manager and destination development officer at Värnamo Municipality. ”We want to give the people of Värnamo and the motorsports community an opportunity to celebrate him together, while also showcasing the strong sense of community and local pride that exists here.”

The event is being jointly organized by Värnamo Näringsliv, Värnamo City and Värnamo Municipality.

“This partnership reflects the strong sense of community that makes Värnamo what it is,” said Anki Hansson of Värnamo Näringsliv. ”Together, we want to create a public celebration that honors Felix while also welcoming visitors to Värnamo.”

Broadcasts Attract 23% Gain Over 2025, 57% Hike Over 2024

FOX Sports announced Sept. 11 its blistering momentum with the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season, averaging 1,681,000 viewers per race, an increase of 23 percent over last year’s full-season average (1,362,000 for 17 races), according to Nielsen Media Research.

The ratings also increased by 57% vs. 2024’s full-season average on NBC (1,073,000 for 16 races), good for the best viewership since 2008. Additionally, FOX INDYCAR scored nine races with at least 1 million viewers, the most since 2008 (10).

Highlights among the events broadcast by FOX were the 110th Running of the Indianapolis 500 (6,635,000 viewers), the Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. (3,282,000), and the XPEL Grand Prix of Road America (1,803,000).

Fast Start, New Events Highlight 2026 Coverage

The FOX INDYCAR season got off the starting line with a stronger schedule than in 2025, slotting in three consecutive races -- and four total – in March, including a doubleheader with NASCAR in Phoenix with the Good Ranchers 250 (1,247,000 viewers) and the debut of the Java House Grand Prix of Arlington (1,336,000 viewers), teaming with the Dallas Cowboys and Texas Rangers on the world-class, Texas-sized event.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C. added a tentpole event of epic proportion in August, with the FOX audience peaking at nearly 3.5 million viewers and delivering media coverage from around the world. The race was the most-watched non-Indianapolis 500 INDYCAR SERIES event since 1995.

Key Demos Continue To Grow

FOX INDYCAR coverage saw a second consecutive year of growth in the coveted P18-49 audience demographic, according to Nielsen Media Research.

The 2026 season finished up 10% vs. 2025 (341,000 vs. 310,000) and up 66% vs. 2024 (205,000). Also in 2026, P25-54 was up 15% vs. last year (412,000 vs. 358,000) and up 63% vs. 2024 (253,000).

Digital Coverage Also Popular

“ALL IN: INDYCAR,” the real-time, season-long documentary series produced by FOX Sports, INDYCAR and Shadow Lion, the critically acclaimed creative studio co-founded by Tom Brady, scored more than 6 million views on YouTube in its first season, averaging nearly 500,000 viewers an episode. The series has been confirmed for a second season in 2027.

Also in 2026, the debut season of “SPEED WITH HARVICK AND BUXTON FUELED BY POET” amassed more than 100 million views on FOX Sports social and digital platforms, making it the fastest ever to hit that mark on FOX Sports platforms. The original digital program also eclipsed 200,000 followers across FOX Sports social and digital platforms.

In August, FOX Sports Digital delivered full coverage of the Freedom 250 across social and editorial, which ranked as the most-viewed non-Indianapolis 500 race week of the INDYCAR SERIES season on social (21 million views) and the highest time spent reading on editorial (5:31).

INDY NXT by Firestone Also Grows Double Digits

The INDY NXT by Firestone season averaged 127,000 viewers (17 races on FS1/FS2), up 14% vs. last year's full-season average (111,000 viewers for 14 races), according to Nielsen Media Research.

The top-three highest-viewership races were Mid-Ohio 1 with 250,000 viewers (July 4), Barber 1 with 191,000 (March 28) and Arlington with 176,000 (March 15).

title: Barry Wanser Weaves Even More Magic With Tight-Knit Palou Tea...
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
A group of brothers is how Barry Wanser, strategist for Alex Palou, describes the No. 10 DHL Chip Ganassi Racing team. It’s a group that guided Palou to his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship and fourth consecutive title this season.

Wanser believes its success goes beyond the numbers. The team has spent the past several seasons learning what makes Palou tick and, more importantly, what he needs to perform at his best.

It’s a recipe everyone tries to replicate but can’t. So, how does this team continue this dominance?

Wanser (photo, top, with Palou) has worked with the No. 10 car since 2004 and has led its race weekend strategy since team owner Chip Ganassi moved to Scott Dixon’s timing stand in 2018. He helped Dan Wheldon win six races and Dario Franchitti win 13 races and three consecutive championships.

Wanser (photo, above) sees something different in Palou that makes him stand out. He sees a driver who understands what he needs from a race car, communicates that to his engineers and adapts when circumstances change.

“It’s the relationship he’s been able to form with the team,” Wanser said. “Specifically with his race engineer, Julian Robertson. That ability that they have to extract and make changes to really get the extra performance out of the car that Alex needs to get the fuel mileage with a lap time to take care of the tires to then go perform at the highest level. Everyone says we’ve made it look easy and stuff. It’s by far not easy.”

Wanser admits Palou’s understanding of the car is just as important. On road and street courses, he knows what the car needs to perform on both the primary and alternate Firestone Firehawk tires. On ovals, he understands the differences between a car built for qualifying and one built for racing.

“Trying to get those done and understand that with the very short amount of practice that we actually get is a challenge,” Wanser said. “That’s something that he’s been able to adapt to in the last few years, especially the oval performance and what it takes.”

A team can give a driver a great car. Engineers can provide the tools, and strategists can make the calls. The driver still must put everything together, and Palou has consistently done that while developing a relationship with the people around him that allows the entire group to function at its highest level.

That was particularly important during the 2026 season. The No. 10 team dealt with strategy missteps, pit-lane speeding, contact with other teams’ equipment and bad pit stops. Each created an opportunity for the championship to slip away.

The team kept recovering.

“It’s really easy to get it wrong, so it’s very hard what we do,” Wanser said. “But for all of Chip Ganassi Racing, the engineers have just really done an incredible job. Everywhere we go, the cars have unloaded very strong, and then it’s up to the individual race engineers with their drivers to extract that extra performance out of the cars, make those changes.”

Palou has 25 career victories, including six in the 2026 season. Wanser believes Palou’s ability to take information, process it and turn it into performance is a major part of that success. Another part is harder to quantify.

Trust.

Palou, Robertson, Wanser and the rest of the No. 10 crew have developed an understanding since Palou joined Chip Ganassi Racing in 2021. They communicate quickly and honestly, which matters in a series where there is little room for error.

Wanser understands that dynamic better than most. He retired from his full-time role as senior manager of racing operations at Chip Ganassi Racing after last season but remained Palou’s strategist. The decision was part of a four- or five-year plan he developed with Ganassi and managing director Mike Hull to mentor Blair Julian and Mike LeGallic and prepare them for greater responsibilities at the Indianapolis shop and at the track.

Wanser (photo, above, white shirt) and his wife, Laurie, moved from Indiana to Florida during last year’s offseason. He and Palou began the 2026 season in Wanser’s new home state on the streets of St. Petersburg, where they won the season opener.

“I take a lot of pride knowing that my family’s plan to move to Florida last year was set in motion four years prior,” Wanser said. “The last time to mentor people, get other people in place, and that’s what you want rather than just say, ‘Hey, the end of this year, I’m going to be moving.’

“So, obviously with what I do on race day, it’s a big part of still the performance of the team. To be able to still be able to do that is an amazing situation for me.

“I’ve been here 29 years, and I’ve been on the 10-car pit stand since 2004. It would be a lot of experience that would just walk away, and I don’t want that.”

Those 29 years have taught Wanser that success is never one person.

Wanser is quick to point out that Ganassi and Palou deserve a higher level of credit, but everyone on the team has a role in allowing the driver to perform at his best. The strategist is simply the person responsible for making the final call.

“For us on the stand, it’s easy,” Wanser said. “I get too much credit as a strategist because it’s not just me. I manage the process. I learned that from Chip many years ago. Yes, ultimately you make the final decision. But generally, we’re constantly talking about strategy, and nine times out of 10, we’re all in agreement what we’re going to do. But sometimes we’re not, and I have to decide.”

That dynamic may be the best explanation for Palou’s remarkable run. His talent is undeniable, but he is surrounded by people he trusts. He listens, communicates and understands what the car needs. Then he goes out and executes at a level that can make one of the most difficult jobs in motorsports look easy.

“We’re a group of brothers,” Wanser said. “We’re having fun. If you say something dumb, you’re going to be made fun of. No one’s off-limits, like myself included. We just have fun.

“If things aren’t going right, we blame each other, kind of thing. But in a fun way, not in an accusing way. Literally, we just roll with it. Everyone knows they’re trying to do the best they can, and we’re having a lot of fun.

“We have no idea how long this amazing amount of success will continue, but we’re just enjoying every bit of it and having fun along the way here.”

Driver News

5 DAYS AGO

Alex Palou completed the second day of INDYCAR’s IR-28 oval validation test Thursday at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, giving engineers another valuable set of data and driver feedback as development continues on the next-generation NTT INDYCAR SERIES car.

The test went so well that Palou (photo, top) ended his running 15 minutes early after the team completed every item on its checklist.

SEE: Alexander Rossi Takes Early Steps Toward Speed With IR-28

“Very fun,” Palou said. “At the beginning, it was super fun because it’s a new car and you’re back at the Speedway. Then you’re like, ‘Can we go faster?’

“It’s still super fun. I’m testing the new car at the Speedway.”

Five-time NTT INDYCAR SERIES champion and 2025 Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge winner Palou (photo, above) was the second driver to experience the IR-28’s oval configuration, following running Wednesday by Alexander Rossi.

Palou and Rossi shared driving duties during the car’s track debut last month on the IMS road course. That three-day test was extended by rain. Rossi, driving for ECR, provided feedback representing Chevrolet teams, while Palou represented Honda teams for Chip Ganassi Racing. Both returned to IMS for the oval validation test.

Rossi completed his testing Wednesday in temperatures that climbed into the low 90s with high humidity. An approaching cold front dropped temperatures nearly 10 degrees Thursday, giving INDYCAR engineers another set of environmental conditions to evaluate the car.

The focus remained on data collection rather than outright speed, despite Palou and Rossi qualifying first and second, respectively, for this year’s Indianapolis 500.

Single-car running allowed engineers to evaluate the IR-28 through a variety of aerodynamic configurations while gathering driver feedback on how the car responds to the demands of oval racing.

Rossi had a separate plan Wednesday than Palou’s checklist Thursday.

The goal of the test was to understand the car’s behavior across different aerodynamic setups and ride heights while identifying opportunities to improve its performance and raceability.

“I don’t really know what he did,” Palou said of Rossi. “I think he did a lot of basic stuff. Even us, we did a lot of basic stuff and trying to get a lot of data for Dallara itself to try and see what the car is doing when we get like crazy ride heights up, down, like just trying to get like basic numbers.”

Considerable development work remains before the IR-28 makes its NTT INDYCAR SERIES race debut in 2028. The two days of oval running at IMS provided another important step in that process, adding data from a variety of aerodynamic configurations and feedback from two Indy 500 winners.

Palou (photo, above) and Rossi now have their first oval impressions of the car that will define the next generation of INDYCAR SERIES racing.

“We got a lot more laps than I expected with the weather, and the car felt good,” Palou said. “We actually got quite a lot of speed. We improved over 2 miles an hour throughout the day, and we didn’t really work too much to get it.”

title: Early Steps Toward Speed Taken With New Car in First Oval Tes...
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
There is plenty that remains unknown about the NTT INDYCAR SERIES’ next-generation car.

Alexander Rossi discovered a little more Wednesday.

SEE: More Smooth Sailing for IR-28 With Alex Palou

On a hot and humid day with temperatures climbing into the low 90s at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, Rossi became the first driver to turn a wheel in the superspeedway configuration of the IR-28 chassis, beginning the next phase of INDYCAR’s development of its new-for-2028 car.

“It does everything that INDYCAR SERIES machinery should do around here,” Rossi said. “We got through some basic mechanical and aero changes to kind of understand the offsets that they're going to present to us in a couple of years, and there was no surprise. It was really pretty standard.”

The test marked the first time the IR-28 has run on an oval after making its public track debut early last month on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course. Rossi and Alex Palou shared driving duties during that initial outing, extended to three days because of rain.

Both drivers are back for this test, with ECR’s Rossi again representing Chevrolet teams and Chip Ganassi Racing’s Palou representing Honda teams, and learning how the car responds to the unique demands of an circle track.

The IR-28 is designed to be lighter than the current car, with revised aerodynamics intended to improve stability and reduce the aerodynamic disadvantage of closely following another car. Wednesday’s laps at IMS provided the first indication of how those objectives translate to an oval.

“The car is doing everything it's supposed to,” said Mike O’Gara, INDYCAR’s vice president of Competition and Race Engineering. “Obviously, Dallara took everything they knew from the DW12 and put it into this car. Immediately, without honestly changing any setup on it, Alex (Rossi) went out and was flat on the throttle and very comfortable.”

That was an encouraging first step, but O’Gara and Rossi each stressed that Wednesday was about gathering information rather than chasing performance.

INDYCAR is approaching the test with a “crawl, walk, run” philosophy, using Rossi’s laps to begin understanding how the car responds to changes before pushing the development further.

That gradual approach is particularly important on an oval.

The current INDYCAR SERIES machinery has been developed for more than a decade, and its superspeedway package is highly refined. The IR-28, meanwhile, is beginning that process from scratch.

Rossi said the IR-28 already feels how an INDYCAR SERIES car should on the 2.5-mile IMS oval, even if there is still considerable work ahead.

“I wouldn't say there was anything drastically different from this car to the current car that we have,” Rossi said. “Some subtle things here and there if you're really nitpicking at it, but, in general, I think it's important to remember that the current-generation Speedway car that we have around here is pretty dialed and it's pretty good.”

That makes Wednesday less about discovering a revolutionary difference and more about identifying the smaller changes that can ultimately shape the 2028 car.

“I don't think that there needs to really be any major glaring issues,” Rossi said. “It's all just early days and trying to get time on it and understanding what little adjustments do here and there. There’s nothing huge separating it from the current car that we have.”

O’Gara said the ease with which 2016 Indianapolis 500 winner Rossi adapted was another positive sign.

“I was just talking to (INDYCAR Officiating technical director) Nick Allen, who's sort of pseudo-crew chief this week, and super happy with how easy the car is to work on,” O’Gara said. “It's very intuitive.”

Rossi’s test day was the first step. 2025 Indianapolis 500 winner Palou takes over Thursday, giving INDYCAR and Dallara another perspective on the car and its potential in “The Greatest Spectacle in Racing.” The feedback from Rossi and Palou will be measured against the data collected by engineers as development continues toward the car’s race debut in 2028.

title: Inside Line: Defining Moment of Alex Palou’s Championship Sea...
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
Featured

6 DAYS AGO

Today’s question: The biggest moment of Alex Palou’s 2025 championship season clearly was his first victory in the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. With no repeat “500” win this year, what was the defining moment of the 2026 championship for the Spaniard, who clinched his fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES title and record-tying fourth in a row?

Curt Cavin: To me, it was that stretch of five races between the Sonsio Grand Prix and the XPEL Grand Prix of Road America when Palou won five consecutive poles (photo, above). That was qualifying domination on two road courses, two ovals and a street circuit, and while he only converted one of them into a race win, he stretched his lead from 17 points to 60 points. Meanwhile, starting on pole each week was delivering psychological blows as opponents were forced to try different strategies in an effort to beat him. Imagine if Palou had won two or three of those races instead of having a five-race average finish of 7.0. He’d have locked up the title much, much sooner than he did.

Eric Smith: To me, his defining moment could be his Long Beach victory, but I’m going with the Nashville win (photo, above). The reason is that, in my opinion, that’s where he unofficially clinched the championship. Palou’s 2026 oval finishes entering Nashville were 24th, seventh and 17th. He had just one finish better than fifth in the previous six races on the season, so the talking point entering that weekend was how much his competition could cut into his championship lead. Second place in points, Kyle Kirkwood, started from the pole and Palou started fourth. Palou though, led 97 of 225 laps and stomped on the hearts of his competitors with not just a solid day, but a victory. He entered Nashville with a 56-point lead and left with an 83-point advantage. In my mind, that effectively sealed the championship.

Arni Sribhen: The tone for Alex Palou’s 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship-winning season was set in March, when he scored podium finishes in three of the first four races – including wins on the streets of St. Petersburg and Barber Motorsports Park (photo, above). Sure, other drivers led the championship in March, but the only thing that kept Palou from a wire-to-wire win was contact that resulted in a DNF at Phoenix. But the latest entry in Palou’s run though INDYCAR history books was again defined by his exceptional consistency set in motion by early dominance. He’s followed that script before, and by the time the rest of the field had figured out who this season’s challengers would be, Palou had already left them behind.

Paul Kelly: The two-race stretch of Nashville and Portland. After Pato O’Ward won on Fourth of July weekend at Mid-Ohio, Alex Palou led Kyle Kirkwood by 65 points with seven races remaining in the season. Palou had won just one of the previous six races, at Detroit, after his sizzling start of three wins from the first five. That led me – and others, I bet – to think, “Maybe we have a title race this season, after all?” Uh, no, we did not. Palou then curb-stomped the field at the next two races, on the oval at Nashville and the road course at Portland (photo, above), leading more than half the laps in each race and taking a 110-point lead in the standings. And just like that, any idea of a championship race was over. Palou didn’t feel quite as dominant for the entire season as he did in 2025, but his spurts like the season-opening run and this summer stretch were more than enough to win the Astor Challenge Cup for the fifth time. And I don’t expect El Rey to hand over his crown in 2027, either.

Scott McLaughlin snapped a 36-race winless drought dating to September 2024 with his victory Sunday in the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

He ended 2026 as hot as any driver in the field, beating Kyle Kirkwood, who placed second to earn his third top-six finish in the final four races of the season.

title: Kelvin Fu To Succeed David Salters as HRC US President
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
Honda Racing Corporation USA (HRC US) has named Kelvin Fu as its next president, succeeding David Salters effective Sept. 12.

Fu (photo, above, left) has long served in senior roles at HRC US, most recently as vice president, and helped lead the organization to four of its 17 Indianapolis 500 victories while in that position.

Salters (photo, above, right) became president of then-Honda Performance Development (HPD) in 2020 and will leave HRC US to join a technology startup outside the motorsports industry.

“When I joined HRC US, I never imagined that one day I would have the privilege of leading this extraordinary organization,” Fu said. “I am truly humbled by the opportunity. Throughout my career at HPD and HRC US, I have been fortunate to work on a wide range of programs, from the development of the NSX GT3, Acura DPi race cars, and the LMDh engine and car to building lasting partnerships with our racing teams.

“Looking ahead, I am excited about the future of HRC US. We recently renewed our commitment to INDYCAR as the series continues to grow and strengthen its position in North American motorsports. Our new business ventures also position us to better serve Honda racing fans. We will remain committed to innovation, competition, and developing the people and technologies that define the future of motorsports. The Honda racing spirit has always been about challenging convention and pushing boundaries, and I look forward to leading HRC US as we write the next chapter of that story together.”

Fu joined HRC US, then known as HPD, in 2015, managing chassis design, aerodynamics and the performance engineering group. He was named director of programs in 2020 before being promoted to vice president in 2021.

Prior to joining Honda, Fu worked primarily in aerospace. He earned bachelor’s and master’s degrees in mechanical engineering from the University of Michigan, followed by a PhD and postdoctoral appointment at the University of California, Berkeley, and another postdoctoral appointment at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. Fu then moved to Los Angeles to join the defense and aerospace company HR Textron.

At HR Textron, Fu served as an R&D engineer and advanced to product manager before moving to ITT Aerospace, where he became director of engineering.

Salters joined HPD in 2015 as chief engineer and engine technical leader before becoming technical director in 2019. Prior to joining HPD, he held a series of roles in other high-profile racing programs, including head of internal combustion engine power unit development for the Ferrari Formula One program, head of Formula One engine development at Mercedes-Benz High-Performance Engines (formerly Ilmor), and development and design engineer for the INDYCAR program at Cosworth Racing Ltd.

During his tenure, Salters oversaw three NTT INDYCAR SERIES manufacturers’ championships and five drivers’ titles. Salters also pioneered the development and modernization of the current hybrid-powered INDYCAR SERIES car, which debuted in 2024.

Additionally, Salters oversaw the launch of the new HRC US business division, which includes apparel, performance parts and a recently announced heritage racing business that connects motorsports collectors with Honda and Acura heritage race cars.

“I would like to say a heartfelt thank you to the marvelous men and women at Honda Racing Corporation USA, our racing teams and talented drivers,” Salters said. “It has been an honor to work together to add to Honda’s racing history here in the U.S.

“Honda Racing gave me and my family the opportunity to come to California 11 years ago. We had the honor of becoming American citizens and have had the most amazing life experience as part of the Honda family.

“HRC US is stronger than ever, with a brilliant team, a very exciting future in INDYCAR and many other cool new projects on the horizon. Now is the perfect time to pass the baton to Kelvin. We have worked closely over the last six years, and Kelvin is the ideal person to support and lead the HRC US team into the future.”

Said Fu: “I want to sincerely thank David Salters for his leadership, friendship and mentorship. Dave challenged all of us to think bigger, move faster and never lose sight of the fact that we are competitors at heart. He is a true racer whose vision and commitment have helped shape HRC US into the world-class organization it is today, and his impact will be felt for many years to come.”

title: Instant Recall: Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
Dueling burnouts Sunday at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca gave the NTT INDYCAR SERIES a proper sendoff to the 2026 season.

The celebrations on the front straightaway were for Alex Palou’s fourth consecutive season championship and fifth title in six years along with Scott McLaughlin’s first race win of the year.

For Palou (photo, above), the eighth-place finish in the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey wasn’t Palou-like given he had won the past two races (and three of the past four) on the 11-turn, 2.238-mile road course, but it was another example of his high-level consistency. Through 18 races over numerous types of tracks, he delivered six wins, 12 top-five and 15 top-10 finishes to win the championship by 86 points. This was the second year in a row that he secured the title in advance of the season’s final race.

For McLaughlin, the victory ended a 36-race drought spanning two years and five days. His last win was Sept. 1, 2024, at the Milwaukee Mile, and this one gave him eight wins for his six full seasons in this series. McLaughlin dominated it, too, leading 87 of 95 laps from the pole. As important is the momentum the performance gives him and the team moving into the offseason as they prepare to challenge Palou’s reign in 2027.

McLaughlin gave Team Penske its third race win of the season. Josef Newgarden won the other two (at Phoenix Raceway and World Wide Technology Raceway). David Malukas was denied the first series victory of his career, but he posted four runner-up finishes during his first season with Roger Penske’s organization and ended with the most points among the team’s drivers. His fifth-place finish in Monterey was his third top-five finish in succession to end the season and ninth overall.

Chip Ganassi Racing’s six wins led all teams this season. Arrow McLaren posted five race wins, three by Pato O’Ward and two by Christian Lundgaard. Andretti Global won three races, two by Kyle Kirkwood and one by Marcus Ericsson. Felix Rosenqvist gave Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian a goodbye victory in his final season with the team, but it was a big one: the 110th Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge, with the most dramatic last lap ever at Indianapolis Motor Speedway.

Kirkwood didn’t lead any laps in the finale and never seriously threatened McLaughlin’s lead in finishing 1.3739 seconds behind him, but it nonetheless was a productive race. Kirkwood overtook Lundgaard for second place in the season standings, and that should be a big confidence boost for the 2021 INDY NXT by Firestone champion heading into his sixth season in this series.

Ed Carpenter Racing’s Alexander Rossi ended the season on a high, grabbing his first podium finish of the year. Finishing a strong and competitive third – he led four laps – gave the Californian his first top-10 finish in the final eight races and provides fodder for preparations for his third season with the organization.

Lundgaard’s sixth-place finish allowed him to become the sixth driver in history to complete all the laps in a season (Scott Dixon did it twice). Lundgaard completed 2,557 laps and finished third in the standings, 13 points ahead of O’Ward. That surely was gratifying given that Arrow McLaren chose not to retain him for next season.

Rosenqvist and Marcus Armstrong each led two laps for MSR, and they finished fourth and seventh in the season finale, respectively. Change is ahead for both drivers and the team as Rosenqvist leaves after three years to return to Arrow McLaren and Armstrong moves into MSR’s lead role – and the No. 60 car that Rosenqvist drove – with Mick Schumacher coming over from one season at Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing to drive the No. 66.

Dixon’s final race with Chip Ganassi Racing ended with a quiet 17th-place finish, and yet it seemed as if their final weekend together after a wildly successful 25-year stint was a celebration of all they accomplished together (58 wins, six series titles). Team owner Chip Ganassi presented the watch-loving Dixon with a special Rolex, and there were hugs and smiles aplenty. They part on good terms, which feels right.

With McLaughlin (photo, above) dominating this final race, there were 24 other drivers and their teams hoping for more, but the season should have many fulfilled. Rinus VeeKay and Juncos Hollinger Racing held onto 10th place in the standings fueled by seven top-10 finishes in the final 11 races to finish with more points than a pair of past series champions (Dixon and Andretti Global’s Will Power).

Dale Coyne Racing’s Dennis Hauger’s season ended in a thud as he got hit from behind on Lap 1 by Sting Ray Robb at Turn 6, but he left the track clutching the Rookie of the Year Award and, perhaps more importantly, will see the seven-figure Leaders Circle bonus for next year that came with finishing in the top 22 of entrant points. That might well allow him to return to Dale Coyne’s team next season.

Ericsson’s ninth-place finish helped him to overtake Newgarden for seventh place in the final standings, 13 positions higher than he finished last year. That’s a win, especially when it included last month’s brilliant drive to take the victory at the new street race in Markham, Ontario. The Swede has five career wins in this series.

The series deserved to be happy with one of its best seasons on record, one that featured an all-timer Indianapolis 500, three terrific new street races, the massively historic Freedom 250 Grand Prix of Washington, D.C., great racing throughout and a champion for the ages.

The field and its fans now take a breath as they await the 2027 season.

title: Paddock Buzz: David Malukas Satisfied With First Penske Seaso...
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
David Malukas hung on to finish fifth in the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey on Sunday, giving him three consecutive top-five finishes to close the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season.

It was Malukas’ ninth top-five finish of the season.

“I think it was really strong for us,” Malukas said. “There’s a few mistakes that we’ve made throughout the weekend that I think we should have started off a bit better. But so many good things to come out of this, especially for me.”

Malukas (photo, top) believes he became a more complete driver in his first season in the No. 12 Verizon Team Penske Chevrolet. Before this season, five of his six career top-five finishes in 61 starts came on ovals. This season, four of his nine top-five finishes came on permanent road courses.

“I think before coming into the season, it was always just ovals only (as my best tracks), and now we figured out the road courses on top of it,” Malukas said. “Street courses still need a little bit more work, but road courses are very strong.”

Malukas’ three consecutive top-five finishes provided a boost after he had three finishes of 12th or worse in a row entering last weekend’s Milwaukee Mile doubleheader.

He believes his tender wrist played a role in that difficult stretch.

Malukas has driven with discomfort since the July 5 race at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course. The pain stems from a left wrist fracture and dislocation, along with torn ligaments, suffered in a mountain biking accident in February 2024.

The pain returned late in Sunday’s 95-lap race, which was slowed by just one caution on the opening lap.

Malukas entered Mid-Ohio second in points but finished the season fifth in the championship.

“I think we were one of the top cars on pace,” Malukas said. “It’s just my wrist started kind of giving out toward the end there.”

Malukas still ended up as the top Team Penske driver in his first season with the team with his fifth-place finish in the standings, easily a career best. His previous best was 11th last season with AJ Foyt Racing.

Team Penske teammates Scott McLaughlin finished sixth in the standings and Josef Newgarden eighth this season.

Kirkwood Finishes Second in Points

Kyle Kirkwood climbed from sixth at the start to finish second in Sunday’s race in the No. 27 Sam’s Club Honda for Andretti Global.

He also finished second in the 2026 standings, 86 points behind champion Alex Palou.

“It’s big,” Kirkwood said. “I hope people consider us as the second-best team. We have a lot to build off of. We made a huge jump year over year. Now second in the championship.

“Will (Power) and Marcus (Ericsson) have come on very strong at the end of the year. We have a lot of momentum going into the offseason. We have a direction. Hopefully we can work on it and better ourselves for next year.”

Kirkwood (photo, above) entered the weekend third in points, two behind Christian Lundgaard. Danish driver Lundgaard climbed from 11th at the start to finish sixth in the No. 7 Arrow McLaren Chevrolet.

Kirkwood ended the season with three top-six finishes in the final four races and 10 top-five finishes in 18 starts.

Dixon’s CGR Tenure Ends

Scott Dixon finished 17th in his 417th and final start with Chip Ganassi Racing.

He didn’t know how he would feel entering the weekend, but the emotions arrived before the race as he prepared to climb into the No. 9 PNC Bank CGR Honda.

“There were definitely many moments,” Dixon said. “I think the race meeting and then probably the pre-race interview and things like that, just kind of seeing old snippets and different memories.”

For the first time since 2004, Dixon (photo, above) failed to win a race, ending his series-record streak of 21 consecutive winning seasons.

Dixon also saw his streak of 20 consecutive seasons finishing in the top six in championship points come to an end. He finished 13th this season, tying 2002 and 2005 for his career-worst points finish.

“Good riddance to the year,” Dixon said. “It was definitely a tough one.”

Mike Hull, the longtime managing director of Chip Ganassi Racing and Dixon’s strategist since 2003, was emotional as he called Dixon’s final race for the team.

“I would say first of all, personally, rather professionally, when you get to ride with a guy like Scott for as long as we have, that’s the team,” Hull said. “For as long as I have, you just stand back in awe of what he does on the racetrack, but better yet, what he does off the racetrack to keep everybody focused.

“To be around greatness, you work your whole life to be around greatness, and when it happens, you just think you’re like a star.”

Hull said the opportunity to work with Dixon has been a career highlight.

“I think understanding that we have a team of people first of all, and a driver that can win, and we’ve managed to be able to do that for a long time,” Hull said. “But the focal point has been Scott Dixon, and we’ve seen other INDYCAR drivers, not very many, that have achieved what he’s achieved over the amount of time that he’s achieved it.

“I always wanted to work in INDYCAR racing. Always wanted to work around people like that, and then having gotten that opportunity, it’s been terrific.”

Odds and Ends

McLaughlin (photo, above) led the first lap of the season on the streets of St. Petersburg and the final lap of the year Sunday at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca.

McLaughlin said this is the first time he’s won a race since becoming a dad. His daughter, Lucy, was born in October 2024. McLaughlin’s last win before today came in September 2024 at Milwaukee Mile.

Team Penske won the season finale for the second straight year. Newgarden won the final race of 2025 at Nashville Superspeedway.

Pato O’Ward finished 11th Sunday in the No. 5 Arrow McLaren Chevrolet and ended up fourth in the final standings. O’Ward has finished in the top five in points in six of his seven full-time seasons, with the worst result being seventh in 2022.

Marcus Ericsson finished ninth in the No. 28 DKY Foundation Honda. That propelled him from eighth to seventh in the final standings, the best the Swede finished since sixth in the three years prior to joining Andretti Global in 2024. The No. 28 car with Andretti hasn’t finished in the top 10 in points since Ryan Hunter-Reay was 10th in 2020.

title: Dennis Hauger Hangs On To Win Tight Rookie of the Year Race
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
Being eliminated from Sunday’s season-ending NTT INDYCAR SERIES race on the first lap at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca left Dennis Hauger in an excruciating position as he watched the rest of the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey.

Hauger (photo, top) was running deep in the 25-car pack as the field bunched approaching Turn 6 when the trailing car of Sting Ray Robb slammed into the back of his, sending the No. 19 Ault Block Chain Honda through the dirt and hard into the tire barrier. The damage proved to be too extensive to repair to continue.

So, Hauger did what he could to pass the time with so much on the line.

“Such a shame,” Hauger said of the early exit and having to wait out the big prizes that stood to elude him. “Obviously, fighting for the (Rookie of the Year) title and the top 22 (in the final standings), and we got taken out after a decent start.

“I don’t know. I think everyone (slowed up) into Turn 6 as they always do (at this track) … I think the guy behind me, I don’t know, closed his eyes for a minute there and went right into the back of me. It’s just such a shame, a bit annoying.”

Forced to accept last place and the five points that go with it, Hauger said he could only “hope for the best.”

That best came – eventually.

Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing’s Mick Schumacher was in 14th position at the time of Hauger’s misfortune, and he needed to get to eighth place to take the spoils from Hauger: the Rookie of the Year Award and next year’s seven-figure Leaders Circle bonus that goes to each of the top 22 finishers from the 2026 season. Schumacher ran as high as 10th position, but he finished 22nd.

Hauger held off Schumacher by 15 points, but he had to sweat it out.

“It's obviously been a bit of a roller coaster this year as a rookie,” Hauger said. “Yeah, to become the Rookie of the Year and get that title is pretty special to me. It can only happen once. To be able to get it, yeah, it's pretty special.”

The 23-year-old Norwegian became the second consecutive INDY NXT by Firestone champion to earn the INDYCAR SERIES rookie award the next year, following Louis Foster of Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing. Prior to Foster, Ed Jones was the last driver to complete the coveted double, in 2017. Linus Lundqvist was Rookie of the Year in 2024, but that was two years after he captured the INDY NXT season title.

Hauger became the third of team owner Dale Coyne’s drivers to win the award, following Alex Lloyd (2010) and Jones. AJ Foyt Racing’s Caio Collet was the third driver in this year’s rookie competition, and he finished 20th in this race.

Hauger, Schumacher (photo, above) and Collet finished the season 22nd, 23rd and 24th in the standings, respectively, evident how competitive they were with one another. They ended up with 25 points from first to third in the rookie category.

Hauger got this season off to a strong start, qualifying in the third position for the opening race in St. Petersburg. That was one of two occasions when he advanced to the Firestone Fast Six, the other coming with a fifth-place effort in Markham, Ontario. He reached the second round of qualifying on road courses or street circuits two other times, giving him four for the season.

“Getting (fourth) in qualifying at Milwaukee was a big surprise,” he said of that oval race. “Did not think that would happen. But overall, there's been some good moments.

“I wouldn't say there's been like any super big surprises, but there's definitely been some good moments and bad moments to take with me from this season. I feel like there was still a lot of points left at the table at times, which is probably one of the things if I went again next year, that would be a big thing to have a look at and think about.

“Coming from P24 to (finish eighth) on the Indy road course was a pretty good moment. That was kind of a surprising moment. Yeah, again, just trying to make the most of every situation we end up in. We've definitely had a few that I guess saved our rookie title in the end.”

Collet (photo, above), a 24-year-old Brazilian, reached the second round of qualifying five times (12th at Indianapolis Motor Speedway, eighth at Road America, 11th each at the Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course and in Washington, and 12th again in this weekend’s session). Schumacher, the 27-year-old son of seven-time Formula One World Champion Michael Schumacher, did so once, in Markham.

Collet led the most laps among this season’s rookies with 16, nine of those earned in the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge where many thought he should have been named Rookie of the Year. Instead, Schumacher received that designation.

Hauger led five laps this season, Schumacher none.

While Hauger’s best qualifying effort was starting third in St. Petersburg, Schumacher’s best was fourth on two occasions (Phoenix Raceway and the second Milwaukee Mile race). Collet’s best was ninth at Road America.

Interestingly, all three rookies had a similar best race result. Hauger and Schumacher each finished eighth – Hauger on the IMS road course, Schumacher at Nashville Superspeedway – while Collet finished ninth in Washington.

The last rookie to win a race was Alexander Rossi in the 2016 Indianapolis 500, but several current drivers, including Graham Rahal, Felix Rosenqvist, Rinus VeeKay, Scott McLaughlin, Christian Lundgaard, Kyle Kirkwood and Christian Rasmussen, won a race in their second year, and Pato O’Ward won a race in his second full season.

While Hauger hopes to return to DCR, Schumacher has been confirmed to join Meyer Shank Racing w/ Curb Agajanian next season, where he will partner with Marcus Armstrong. They were teammates in 2018 at PREMA Racing in the Formula 3 European Championship, with Schumacher taking the title and Armstrong finishing fifth, two positions ahead of Alex Palou, who Sunday capped his fourth consecutive NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship and fifth in six years. Hauger won the FIA F3 European title in 2021, also with PREMA.

Like Hauger, Collet’s plans for 2027 have not yet been confirmed.

title: Scott McLaughlin Ends Drought With Dominant Laguna Seca Win
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
Scott McLaughlin ended a long winless streak and the 2026 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season in style, dominating the Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey for his first victory in more than two years.

Pole sitter McLaughlin (photo, above) drove the No. 3 DEX Team Penske Chevrolet to victory by 1.3739 seconds over the No. 27 Sam’s Club Honda of Andretti Global’s Kyle Kirkwood. The win was the eighth of McLaughlin’s INDYCAR SERIES career and his first since Sept. 1, 2024, in the second race of a doubleheader weekend at the Milwaukee Mile, snapping a drought of 36 races.

SEE: Race Results

“My little girl (Lucy, born in October 2024) hasn’t seen me win yet, and now she has,” McLaughlin said. “So, Dad’s coming home with a trophy, baby. Let’s go!

“These guys and girls at Team Penske have stood behind me the whole time. Congrats to Alex (Palou) on his fifth (championship), but we’re working hard to beat them, and today was a big step in the right direction.”

Alexander Rossi finished third in the No. 20 Java House ECR Chevrolet for his first podium finish since placing third at this event for Arrow McLaren in June 2024.

Felix Rosenqvist placed fourth in the No. 60 Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian Honda. David Malukas put two Team Penske cars in the top five in the No. 12 Verizon Team Penske Chevrolet.

Alex Palou punctuated the fifth NTT INDYCAR SERIES championship that he clinched last weekend at Milwaukee with a quiet drive to eighth place in the No. 10 DHL Lightning Bolt Honda of Chip Ganassi Racing after he won this race the last two years. But Palou and the CGR team celebrated its record-tying fourth consecutive season title with donuts on the front straightaway by the driver and again in a boisterous post-race Astor Challenge Cup presentation (photo, above).

McLaughlin left absolutely no doubt about his dominance in this race on the 11-turn, 2.238-mile road course. He only trailed during pit stop sequences and ended up leading 87 of 95 laps, erasing all memories of the six podium finishes without a win since his last triumph.

There was only one caution period in the race, for a Lap 1 incident in which Sting Ray Robb’s No. 77 Juncos Hollinger Racing – Goodheart Chevrolet hit the rear of Dennis Hauger’s No. 19 Ault Block Chain Honda of Dale Coyne Racing in Turn 6, sending Hauger spinning into the tire barrier.

McLaughlin had no problem pulling away from the field on the restart on Lap 4, and his precise driving and Team Penske’s clean, quick work during three pit stops took care of the rest.

“We had to be solid,” McLaughlin said. “That’s what it’s going to take to win a championship. What a great warmup we had. Bring on 2027.”

Kirkwood, who started sixth, had climbed to second by Lap 20 after Palou pitted to switch to a different tire strategy and shadowed McLaughlin for the rest of the way, pitting at the same time as McLaughlin on all three stops. McLaughlin’s lead was nearly four seconds at the halfway point, but Kirkwood pulled as close as 1.2 seconds on Lap 72 due to running his final stint on the faster but less-durable Firestone Firehawk alternate tire.

But McLaughlin eased away in the closing laps on the more durable Firestone primary tire, as Kirkwood admitted he and the Andretti Global team took a safety-first approach to ensure the driver would finish a career-best second in the standings. Kirkwood ended up 86 points behind champion Palou.

“Second in the championship, and that’s my best road-course finish,” Kirkwood said. “We just played it super clean, super methodical. I wish I could have had a go at Scotty there at the end on the better tires, but we knew who we were fighting, and that was for the championship, mostly. So, we played it safe there. Second place is best of the rest.”

2016 Indianapolis 500 winner Rossi also was a fixture in the top three for most of the race, producing the best day for ECR since teammate Christian Rasmussen won in August 2025 at Milwaukee. Rasmussen also finished third this year at World Wide Technology Raceway, but road courses have been a weak spot for ECR this season. The best previous finish on this type of circuit was sixth by Rossi in June at Road America.

“I don’t think I could state the significance of it just with how challenging this year has been for the whole organization and how much road courses have been a huge struggle of ours,” Rossi said. “There was a lot of doubt coming into this event whether we could find a direction, so I think this is just a huge reward for all the effort.”

Despite finishing last in the 25-car field due to the incident with Robb, Hauger hung on to win series Rookie of the Year honors. He finished with 228 points, 15 ahead of Mick Schumacher of Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing in the rookie race.

The 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES season opens Sunday, March 7 on the streets of St. Petersburg, Florida.

Their starting positions will be adjusted when penalties are handed out for unapproved engine changes, but Lundgaard’s car is one of those which will be moving six positions deeper in the field.

For Lundgaard (photo, top), finishing second in the standings is a matter of pride on several fronts. “I think we've been extremely good this year at dodging all the accidents and the situations you don't want to put yourself in,” he said. “Sometimes in hindsight, it probably hurt more than it than it helped. But yeah, it would be pretty cool if we could finish all of it.”

With this 11-turn, 2.238-mile circuit a permanent road course, it’s worth noting that Lundgaard leads all drivers this season in points scored on such tracks. “I don’t know if I’m much better, but I definitely know that the (team’s) road course package is better,” Lundgaard said of a year-over-year improvement. “(The season has been) better than any other year, clearly.

“Obviously, if we can beat the guy consistently in the last half of the season, that's been the unbeatable driver and won four championships in a row. I think we've done pretty well.”

It’s fitting that the three top contenders for the runner-up position are among the multiple race winners this season. O’Ward has three wins, including both ends of last weekend’s doubleheader at the Milwaukee Mile, while Lundgaard and Kirkwood have two each.

“It’s more just surviving,” he said Saturday. “For me, I’ve got two days left here where we’re testing a lot of good stuff with the car (for next year). Qualifying is easy on the wrist – you only push for two laps and then you get to recover. But these races always take a toll.”

Driver News

SEP 05, 2026

Dreyer & Reinbold Racing (DRR) announced Sept. 5 that Conor Daly has signed a multiyear agreement to drive the team’s new full-time No. 24 entry in the NTT INDYCAR SERIES beginning in 2027,

In addition, DRR also announced the team will field Honda engines in the 2027 NTT INDYCAR SERIES. The organization previously used Honda engines in the series from 2005-11.

“I am extremely grateful to get back to full-time INDYCAR racing with my friends at Dreyer and Reinbold Racing and Honda,” Daly said. “The faith that this group has shown in me is something that makes me want to work harder than ever before to deliver. We, as a team, will aim every day to make Dennis (Reinbold) proud of the effort we put in to be competitive and continue the team’s legacy.”

DRR will return to the NTT INDYCAR SERIES full time for the 2027 campaign for the first time since 2012 when Oriol Servia drove the team’s lone entry. On July 22, DRR announced the team had purchased one NTT INDYCAR SERIES charter from Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing for its 2027 full-time series return.

The DRR team, established in 1999, continues the 100-year legacy of the Dreyer and Reinbold families in open-wheel racing dating back to DRR team owner Dennis Reinbold’s grandfather, the legendary Floyd “Pop” Dreyer, who served as a mechanic for the Duesenberg team in the 1920s. Dreyer was also a renowned race car builder, constructing cars for the entire 1931 Indy 500 front row. Reinbold passed away June 13.

DRR has been a participant in the legendary Indianapolis 500 since 2000, with 58 drivers qualifying for the famed “The Greatest Spectacle in Racing.”

Daly also returns to full-time action after 133 NTT INDYCAR SERIES starts during his career dating back to his series debut in 2013 in the Indy 500. The veteran driver has a best series finish of second at Detroit in 2016. Daly also won a pole position at Iowa Speedway in 2020.

The Indianapolis-area native has made two Indy 500 starts with Dreyer & Reinbold Racing, in 2024 and 2026, finishing 10th and 12th, respectively, and leading 26 laps in the races.

“Dreyer & Reinbold Racing is returning to full-time competition in 2027 with Honda engines, and Conor Daly is the driver we want leading that return,” said Derek Reinbold, DRR CEO. “Conor has raced for us at Indianapolis, so we know how he prepares, how he works with engineers and how much he gets out of a car. He has shown for years that he can win the Indianapolis 500, and our job is to give him a car that lets him do it.

“We are building a team that contends every weekend, and Conor is the driver we trust to carry that effort across the full season. An Indiana driver in an Indiana team’s car is exactly how we want to come back.”

Pato O’Ward arrived at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca with a chance to cap his season with a milestone he has never achieved in his NTT INDYCAR SERIES career – three consecutive victories.

O’Ward (photo, top) swept last weekend’s Milwaukee Mile doubleheader and moved from fifth to fourth in the championship standings. “A lot of Pato fans are going to be pumped,” O’Ward said.

A third consecutive victory would also give O’Ward his first podium finish at Laguna Seca.

O’Ward enters the season finale with 12 career NTT INDYCAR SERIES victories, including three this season. Remarkably, those three wins account for all his podium finishes in 17 starts in the No. 5 Arrow McLaren Chevrolet in 2026.

The Mexican has recorded 10 top-five finishes, putting him second best behind Alex Palou’s 12. But O’Ward has just the three podium finishes compared to Palou’s seven.

A victory Sunday would give O’Ward four wins in a season for the first time in his career and make him the first driver to win three consecutive races since Palou last season at Barber Motorsports Park, the Sonsio Grand Prix and the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

O’Ward has made five starts at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca, with a best finish of fourth last year. He also finished fifth in 2021.

He showed immediate speed on a sun-drenched California Friday, finishing third quickest in opening practice as he looks to carry his Milwaukee momentum into the season finale -- and potentially make one last push for second in the championship.

“Second place (in points) matters,” O’Ward said. “It means a bigger bonus.”

Rosenqvist’s MSR Tenure Nearing End

Several drivers enter this weekend knowing they will make their final starts with their current teams.

Among them are Chip Ganassi Racing’s Scott Dixon, who joins Arrow McLaren in 2027, and Meyer Shank Racing’s Felix Rosenqvist, who also will move to Arrow McLaren next season. Rosenqvist and Dixon join O’Ward at the team famous for its papaya colors.

Rosenqvist’s two-year tenure at MSR has marked a significant turnaround for the organization.

He joined the team in 2024 after three seasons with Arrow McLaren from 2021-23 and two seasons with Chip Ganassi Racing from 2019-20. Rosenqvist helped MSR climb from 25th in entrant points before his arrival to 12th in his first season and sixth last year.

This season, he gave MSR its first victory since Helio Castroneves won the 2021 Indianapolis 500 when Rosenqvist made a pass just ahead of the checkered flag to win this year’s Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge.

Rosenqvist (photo, above) enters Laguna Seca ninth in the championship and was second quickest in Friday’s opening practice.

“Pretty good session for us,” Rosenqvist said. “Good on both (tire) compounds, which is always nice. A little bit of an emotional weekend last weekend with the team. Obviously, we've known this for a long time, but it's definitely gone quick since I announced I was leaving.

“Excited for the future. Always a lot on your mind when you know you're going to leave a good group, a lot of good people, friendships and so on. We all said the best thing we can do is go out and try to win and have some fun, as well. It's kind of a no-pressure weekend in the way.”

Rosenqvist has two top-five finishes in six starts at Laguna Seca, including a best finish of fourth in 2022. He also won the pole in 2023.

Zanardi Honored

WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca began Friday by dedicating the famous Corkscrew turn complex as the “Zanardi Corkscrew,” honoring the late Alex Zanardi and commemorating the 30th anniversary of his pass that became one of the defining moments of his remarkable career.

On Sept. 8, 1996, Zanardi made a daring move in the No. 4 Target Chip Ganassi Racing Honda by diving under Bryan Herta entering the Turn 8 Corkscrew on the final lap of the CART season finale at Laguna Seca.

The ceremony gathered special guests from throughout Zanardi’s career, including team owner Chip Ganassi, friend and competitor Max Papis, INDYCAR President J. Douglas Boles and other INDYCAR SERIES legends (photo, above), as the motorsports community reflected on the moment that forever connected Zanardi to Laguna Seca.

A commemorative marker recognizing the Zanardi Corkscrew was unveiled during the ceremony, linking Zanardi’s name with Turn 8 at the Central California Coast circuit. A sign featuring the car in which he made the famous pass also was placed outside the corner (photo, above).

Jimmy Vasser clinched the team’s first championship that day. But Ganassi said it was Zanardi who stole the spotlight.

“In typical Zanardi fashion, he stole the show,” Ganassi said. “He stole the show and stole my heart.”

The move became known as “The Pass.” Thirty years later, it remains one of the most recognized moments in Laguna Seca and American open-wheel racing history.

Ganassi compared it to iconic moments in sports, from Joe Montana to Dwight Clark’s “The Catch” to Michael Jordan’s “The Shot” and the Pittsburgh Steelers’ “Immaculate Reception.”

“Alex Zanardi gave us one of those moments that day,” Ganassi said.

CGR Managing Director Mike Hull said the moment made Zanardi “larger than life.”

But Zanardi’s legacy extends far beyond one corner. A two-time CART champion in 1997 and 1998, and winner of 15 CART races, he became one of the sport’s most beloved drivers.

After a devastating 2001 accident at the Lausitzring resulted in the loss of both legs, Zanardi returned to racing and later became a champion hand cyclist and Paralympic gold medalist.

“Alex turned a disability into an ability,” Papis said.

Zanardi died May 1 at age 59.

His namesake corner joins the Turn 2 “Andretti Hairpin” and the “Rahal Straight” at Laguna Seca.

Odds and Ends

Rock band Nickelback will be on-site for Sunday’s season finale, with band members Chad Kroeger, Ryan Peake, Mike Kroeger and Daniel Adair joining MSR to see the No. 60 Meyer Shank Racing w/Curb Agajanian Honda and its new livery featuring the band in person. In addition, Nickelback also will serve as grand marshal and will give the command.

Lundgaard and rookie Caio Collet each will have a six-position grid penalty for Sunday’s race. Both incurred the penalties for unapproved engine changes following the two races at Milwaukee Mile on Sunday, Aug. 30.

Last weekend’s doubleheader at Milwaukee Mile averaged 950,000 viewers, making it the most-watched Milwaukee race weekend since 2011. The audience was up 22 percent from the 2025 race (780,000). This season is averaging 1,731,000 viewers through 17 races, up 27 percent from last year’s 1,362,000 through 17 races, the first season FOX Sports aired the NTT INDYCAR SERIES.

Chip Ganassi Racing’s transporters received an update this weekend, with a new graphic featuring 18 NTT INDYCAR SERIES championships. The latest addition represents Palou’s fifth championship, secured last weekend. Palou has won five titles in the last six years, including four consecutive championships.

source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
As Scott Dixon prepared for his final race weekend as a Chip Ganassi Racing driver, he spoke of moments he will carry to the next stage of his career and his life – 25 years of relationships with people who have come, gone and largely remained in Chip Ganassi’s organization.

Friends, he called them Friday.

“Twenty-five years,” Dixon said in reflection at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca, site of Sunday’s Mission Foods Grand Prix of Monterey (2:30 p.m. ET, FOX, FOX Deportes, FOX One, INDYCAR Radio powered by OnlyBulls). “It’s been fantastic, and it’s been a lot of fun with all those people. We’ll continue to all be friends, and obviously I’m not going far. I’ll see them next year, and you know, just be in a slightly different environment.”

Interestingly, Dixon will almost be able to see CGR’s longtime headquarters from his new digs at Arrow McLaren. Both race shops are located within a block of one another on Indianapolis’ northwest side.

As the 46-year-old father of three continued, Dixon mentioned incredibly close ties not only with team owner Chip Ganassi but also managing director Mike Hull, who almost exclusively has been the voice in his ear since joining the team in 2002. Yes, they have won 58 NTT INDYCAR SERIES races and six season championships together, but it’s the time away from the track that made them family long before Dixon and his wife, Emma, created a family of their own.

Dixon spoke of staying at Ganassi’s home and meeting his lifelong friends, and there was the time team sponsor PNC Bank took members of the organization into the desert to race buggies. Ganassi was a passenger in one of the cars, and his stomach couldn’t handle it.

Dixon laughed about how poorly Ganassi fared, an example of the fun they had together.

“Race wins and things like that are obvious (highlights),” he said. “But those (friendships) are the moments that I’ll remember, and they’re not necessarily (moments) at the track.”

It’s reasonable to say there has never been – nor will there likely ever be – another INDYCAR SERIES pairing such as this one. Not only was it a record for duration, their results rank atop nearly every category in U.S. open-wheel racing history.

For example, this weekend’s race will be their 417th as one. That alone would be enough to hold the sport’s record, and a host of other career marks Dixon owns, including consecutive series starts (373) and most consecutive winning seasons (21), all have been earned as a CGR driver.

Dixon also leads all drivers in history in winning seasons, top-three finishes and top-five finishes. He would still own those records with his rookie season with PacWest Racing in 2001 factored out. Similarly, Dixon would still be No. 2 all-time in race wins and laps led solely as a CGR driver.

All 28 of Dixon’s poles, including 12 wins from the top qualifying position, were accomplished with Ganassi’s team, all with Hull on his pit box.

Dixon joined Ganassi’s Indianapolis-based organization in 2002 – before current series drivers Louis Foster, Dennis Hauger, Nolan Siegel and Kyffin Simpson were born. Their debut was the fourth race of Champ Car’s season, at the Milwaukee Mile. Dixon qualified fourth and finished sixth. But most people won’t remember that Dixon drove the team’s No. 44 car (photo, above), and coincidentally finished one position behind the No. 9 car driven by Team Rahal’s Michel Jourdain Jr.

CGR switched to the Indy Racing League for the 2003 season, and Dixon was issued No. 9. He has driven with that number for all but 15 races since then, those coming in a disastrous 2004 season when he carried No. 1 as the reigning series champion. Dixon finished the year 10th in the point standings and was held out of the July 25 race at Milwaukee following accidents in practice and qualifying. He has not missed a race since.

The Dixon-CGR pairing set a bar for excellence in the Indianapolis 500 presented by Gainbridge. In addition to winning the 2008 race, they won five poles, one shy of Rick Mears’ record. They have finished in the top five nine times and hold the event record for laps led with 709. Dixon led 32 laps in this year’s race, the 17th time he has led in 24 starts. Seven times he has led 50 or more laps, which equates to more than a quarter of those races.

Dixon’s best season with CGR came in 2008 when he won Indy (photo, above) and the series title. All told, he won six races and six poles.

The Kiwi likely would be tied with A.J. Foyt for the most season titles in history if not for running out of fuel on the final lap of the 2007 season at Chicagoland Speedway. Dario Franchitti did well to avoid running into the back of Dixon’s race-leading car as it sputtered in Turn 3. That situation gave Franchitti the race win and the first of his four series championships.

Dixon has won three consecutive races on three different occasions (in 2007, 2013 and 2020).

Graham Rahal has the second-longest active tenure with one team (14 years), but he will need to still be with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing in 2037 to match the Dixon-CGR partnership.

Will Power, who left Team Penske last year after 17 consecutive seasons, marveled at what Dixon and CGR have done together.

“It just shows you the level of talent, absolute professionalism,” Power said Friday. “It will be strange to see someone else in (the No. 9 car).”

During Power’s last race with Team Penske last August at Nashville Superspeedway, he noticed he was parked behind Andretti Global’s No. 26 car driven by Colton Herta.

“That’s the car I’ll be in next year, that’s the crew,” Power remembered thinking.

That could be Dixon this weekend. In 2027, his car will be papaya rather than orange as a new era begins.

title: Favorites and Sleepers: Laguna Seca
source: Latest NTT INDYCAR SERIES News and Results | Official Site of INDYCAR
excerpt:
Honda boasts a perfect 6-for-6 record at WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca since the NTT INDYCAR SERIES returned to the Northern California road course in 2019.

Alex Palou has won three of the past four races, with Chip Ganassi Racing teammate Scott Dixon winning the other in 2023. Palou (car photo, top) also won the most recent permanent road course race of the season at Portland International Raceway before clinching his fifth championship last weekend at Milwaukee Mile.

Colton Herta won the other two races at Laguna Seca, driving in 2019 for Harding Steinbrenner Racing and 2021 with Andretti Global.

Can anyone dethrone top Honda teams Chip Ganassi Racing or Andretti Global in Sunday’s Mission Grand Prix of Monterey, airing at 2:30 p.m. ET on FOX, FOX One, FOX Deportes and INDYCAR Radio powered by OnlyBulls?

Favorites

Scott McLaughlin (No. 3 DEX Team Penske Chevrolet)

McLaughlin has three top-10 finishes in his past four Monterey starts, including a runner-up result in 2023. The New Zealand native has seven top-eight finishes in the last nine races on the season, too.

Pato O’Ward (No. 5 Arrow McLaren Chevrolet)

O’Ward has finished fifth, eighth, ninth, eighth and fourth, respectively, in his five Monterey starts. He won at Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course, a comparable track, in July and has scored the sixth-most permanent road course points this season. O’Ward enters Laguna Seca after sweeping both Milwaukee races last Sunday.

Christian Lundgaard (No. 7 Arrow McLaren Chevrolet)

Lundgaard has a seventh-place average finish in four Laguna Seca starts, with results of fifth, sixth and 15th, respectively, in three starts with Rahal Letterman Lanigan Racing and a runner-up finish last year in his first season with Arrow McLaren.

He won this season on the 2.439-mile, 14-turn Indianapolis Motor Speedway road course and at Road America. Lundgaard was runner-up at Barber and Mid-Ohio. He leads all drivers in permanent road course points this season, six more than Palou.

Alex Palou (No. 10 DHL Lightning Bolt Honda)

Palou has never finished worse than third in five Laguna Seca starts, with a 1.6 average finish. He has led 250 laps, including 67 in 2022, 51 in 2023, 48 in 2024 and 84 of 95 last year.

He is a three-time winner and two-time pole winner at Laguna Seca, including winning both the pole and race the last two years. Palou has five top-five finishes in five permanent road course starts this season.

Will Power (No. 26 TWG AI Honda)

Power has five top-seven finishes in six Laguna Seca starts, including second in 2019, third in 2022, fourth in 2023 and seventh the last two years. He has three top-six finishes in his past three permanent road course starts this season, which equates to the fifth-most permanent road course points accumulated.

Sleepers

Josef Newgarden (No. 2 Astemo Team Penske Chevrolet)

Newgarden finished 10th, fourth, 22nd, ninth and eighth on natural road courses this season and has four top-11 finishes in six Monterey starts. He was runner-up in 2022.

The sleeper designation comes because he hasn’t won on a road course since 2022 at Road America.

Romain Grosjean (No. 18 BMax Honda)

Grosjean has a 6.3 average finish at Laguna Seca, with results of third, seventh, 11th and fourth, respectively, in four starts.

Alexander Rossi (No. 20 ECR Java House Chevrolet)

Rossi has four top-10 finishes in six Laguna Seca starts, three of them in the last four years, including a third-place finish in 2024. He finished sixth this season at Road America.

Kyle Kirkwood (No. 27 Sam’s Club Honda)

Kirkwood swept the 2021 INDY NXT by Firestone weekend at Laguna Seca, but he has one top-10 finish in four INDYCAR SERIES starts, with a 16.8 average finish. He was 21st in 2022 with AJ Foyt Racing and finished 25th, fifth and 16th, respectively, in three starts with Andretti Global.

Kirkwood has finished fifth, ninth, 10th, third and fifth on permanent road courses this season, totaling 137 points, fourth among all drivers.

Rinus VeeKay (No. 76 Juncos Hollinger Racing Chevrolet)

VeeKay has finished fourth in each of the past two permanent road course races this season. He has six top-seven finishes in the last nine races.
